title: My management game’s HUD was a mess. We drew five other options. Which would you ship?
author: Don_InterestingSys
selftext:
I'm making Under Management, a 3D dungeon-management game: you dig out a house, hire staff, and defend the gold from adventurers. There are no unit orders, so during a raid you need to \*watch the action\*

And the screen was fighting you: 398 words of panels, logs and widgets.

So we mocked five replacements over the same screenshot, each played through calm → raid → pause → a "show everything" key:

Out of 50 iterations these stood out as the best

\- A · Figures on the house. Every number sits on the thing it measures (gold on the hoard, heat on the fire, the raid countdown on its road). One small page of notes. 82 words calm / 45 in a raid.

\- B · One rule, one line. Four fixed figures in a corner, one note at a time. 54 / 27.

\- C · One open page. Everything on one sheet that turns when the bell rings. 85 / 49.

\- D · Whatever he's holding. The deputy's pen, watch, ledger or lamp decides what's shown. 87 / 60.

\- E · Tags tied to things. Paper dockets tied to rooms and staff, nothing at the screen's edges. 74 / 37.

I know which way I'm leaning... but I liked the old interface every step along the way that it went from simple to cluttered mess until one day a play tester said it was a mess, so, yeah, I could use help

(The numbers and names in the mocks are placeholders. The tool menu is trimmed in all five, so the real word counts will be a bit higher. The mocks were drawn with Claude Fable 5.2 from a shared brief and ate half of my weekly subscription; happy to share the prompts.  The build will go via Opus 5.5)
